drills.coachNote: White wanted exactly this: swing the knight from e5 to g6, hitting your queen on e7 and rook on f8 at once. You played f6 hoping to kick the knight off e5, but that doesn't stop it jumping to g6 — it just escapes into a bigger threat, and after Ng6 Qf7 Nxf8 Rxf8 you're down the exchange, rook for knight. Rfe8 solves it simply: get the rook off f8 first so there's nothing to fork, then meet Nf3 with Qd7 and trade down calmly. drills.coachNote: White wants to trade on d4 and swing the queen to g4, hitting your weak g7 pawn while your king is still stuck on e8, unable to castle. Your knight jump to d4 looked natural, but Nxd4 exd4 Qg4 forces exactly that — g7 is suddenly hanging with only your queen able to cover it, and Qf6 costs you tempo and any smooth development, a swing of nearly two pawns. Ne7 keeps the knight flexible without opening d4 as a trading square; after c4 g6 Qb3 Rb8 d4 you get to castle with the center still closed.
